page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.large is an entry-level virtual server within the High Clock Speed family, designed for compute-bound tasks requiring high frequency per core. Operating on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The hardware allotment provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core across 2 threads, supported by a 33 MB Level 3 cache, 1.0 MB Level 2 cache, and 32 KB Level 1 data cache per core. The configuration includes AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside AES cryptography acceleration. Memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 0 GB of bundled local storage, necessitating remote cloud disks for persistent data, and does not feature GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is configured with a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations highlight a distinct split between single-threaded efficiency and overall parallel throughput. The 3.3 GHz Intel core achieves average-tier performance in single-threaded tests, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1308.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 1571.78, and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 27.02 GB/sec. However, because execution relies on a single hyperthreaded core, multi-threaded metrics rank in the lower percentiles across testing suites. Geekbench multi-core registers at 1579.0, PassMark CPU score reaches 2543.29, and stress-ng multi-core sits at 2067.69. Memory bandwidth tests yield 15.84 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 13.29 GB/sec for writes. Similarly, static web throughput reaches 2.5 GB/sec and Redis SET operations attain 2.05 million operations per second, reflecting the scale of the 2 vCPU allocation.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, ecs.hfc7.large offers a cost-effective allocation of high-clock-speed CPU capacity without the resource overhead of larger memory arrays or higher core counts. The primary tradeoff lies in its limited parallel scaling: tasks bound by single-thread frequency execute steadily, but high concurrency, large in-memory workloads, and heavy parallel compilation will experience bottlenecks. This server configuration is best aligned with lightweight web application servers, microservices, small CI/CD runner jobs, single-threaded batch processing, and script automation tasks that comfortably fit within the 4.0 GB memory envelope.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.large is a high-clock-speed compute-oriented instance powered by a 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading, the instance includes 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage, requiring external block volumes, and includes no GPU hardware. Performance evaluation reveals solid single-threaded capabilities, reflected in average tier scores across stress-ng single-core execution, Geekbench single-core benchmarks, and single-threaded gzip compression. In contrast, aggregate multi-core computational throughput, uncached memory bandwidth, and static web serving speeds remain constrained by the low core count. The instance delivers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused duties where execution speed per thread is critical, making it suitable for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch processing, utility automation, and small-scale application hosting.
